arxiv-2104-03325.title: Swampland Conjectures and Infinite Flop Chains
arxiv-2104-03325.creator: Callum R. Brodie, Andrei Constantin, Andre Lukas, Fabian Ruehle
arxiv-2104-03325.description: Abstract We investigate swampland conjectures for quantum gravity in the context of M-theory compactified on Calabi-Yau threefolds which admit infinite sequences of flops. Naively, the moduli space of such compactifications contains paths of arbitrary geodesic length traversing an arbitrarily large number of Kähler cones, along which the low-energy spectrum remains virtually unchanged.

arxiv-2207-02681.title: Directional transport of active particles confined in 3 ​ D 3D (three dimensional) smooth corrugated channel
arxiv-2207-02681.creator: Bing Wang, Wenfei Wu
arxiv-2207-02681.description: Abstract The transport phenomenon of active particles confined in 3 ​ D 3D (three dimensional) corrugated confined channel with Gaussian noises is investigated. Large noise intensity perpendicular to the symmetry axis is good for the diffusion and current along the axis. The generalized resonance transport phenomenon appears with increasing noise intensity parallel to the symmetry axis.

arxiv-2211-05432.title: Speech Enhancement with Fullband-Subband Cross-Attention Network
arxiv-2211-05432.creator: Jun Chen, Wei Rao, Zilin Wang, Zhiyong Wu, Yannan Wang, Tao Yu, Shidong Shang, Helen Meng
arxiv-2211-05432.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jun Chen, Wei Rao, Zilin Wang, Zhiyong Wu, Yannan Wang, Tao Yu, Shidong Shang, Helen Meng. FullSubNet has shown its promising performance on speech enhancement by utilizing both fullband and subband information. However, the relationship between fullband and subband in FullSubNet is achieved by simply concatenating the output of fullband model and subband units. It only supplements the subband units with a small quantity of global information and has not considered the interaction between fullband and subband.

arxiv-2403-06816.title: Efficient first-order algorithms for large-scale, non-smooth maximum entropy models with application to wildfire science
arxiv-2403-06816.creator: Gabriel P. Langlois, Jatan Buch, Jérôme Darbon
arxiv-2403-06816.description: Abstract Maximum entropy (Maxent) models are a class of statistical models that use the maximum entropy principle to estimate probability distributions from data. Due to the size of modern data sets, Maxent models need efficient optimization algorithms to scale well for big data applications.

arxiv-2411-03094.title: Linear response in a charged gas in curved spacetime and covariant heat equation
arxiv-2411-03094.creator: Long Cui, Xin Hao, Liu Zhao
arxiv-2411-03094.description: Abstract We consider the linear response of a near-equilibrium charged relativistic gas in the presence of electromagnetic and gravitational field in a generic stationary spacetime up to the second order of relaxation time and calculate the tensorial kinetic coefficients introduced by the presence of the strong electromagnetic and/or gravitational field.

arxiv-2506-13528.title: Microphysical Origins of Gravitational Potentials in Astrophysical Systems
arxiv-2506-13528.creator: Meir Shimon
arxiv-2506-13528.description: Abstract Most astrophysical systems (except for very compact objects such as, e.g., black holes and neutron stars) in our universe are characterized by shallow gravitational potentials, with dimensionless compactness | Φ | ≡ r s / R ≪ 1 \left|\Phi\right|\equiv r_{s}/R\ll 1 , where r s r_{s} and R R are their Schwarzschild radius and typical size, respectively.

arxiv-2510-08415.title: Stochastic Volatility-in-mean VARs with Time-Varying Skewness Corresponding author: Haroon Mumtaz ( h.mumtaz@qmul.ac.uk ). The views expressed in this paper are those of the authors and do not represent those of the European Central Bank, the Central Bank of Brazil, or any of their Committees.
arxiv-2510-08415.creator: Leonardo N. Ferreira, Haroon Mumtaz, Ana Skoblar
arxiv-2510-08415.description: Abstract This paper introduces a Bayesian vector autoregression (BVAR) with stochastic volatility-in-mean and time-varying skewness. Unlike previous approaches, the proposed model allows both volatility and skewness to directly affect macroeconomic variables. We provide a Gibbs sampling algorithm for posterior inference and apply the model to quarterly data for the US and the UK.

pmc-10608275.title: Anti-CD20 Antibody and Calcineurin Inhibitor Combination Therapy Effectively Suppresses Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Murine Orthotopic Lung Transplantation
pmc-10608275.creator: Hiroki Matsumoto, Hidemi Suzuki, Takahiro Yamanaka, Taisuke Kaiho, Atsushi Hata, Terunaga Inage, Takamasa Ito, Toshiko Kamata, Kazuhisa Tanaka, Yuichi Sakairi, Shinichiro Motohashi, Ichiro Yoshino, Ryuichi Waseda, So Miyahara
pmc-10608275.description: Antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) is a risk factor for chronic lung allograft dysfunction, which impedes long-term survival after lung transplantation. There are no reports evaluating the efficacy of the single use of anti-CD20 antibodies (aCD20s) in addition to calcineurin inhibitors in preventing AMR. Thus, this study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of aCD20 treatment in a murine orthotopic lung transplantation model.

pmc-11455447.creator: Stefanie Parisien-La Salle, Guy Van Vliet, Gilles Corbeil, Marjorie Labrecque, Martine Tétreault, Isabelle Bourdeau
pmc-11455447.description: Disclosure: S. Parisien-La Salle: None. G. Van Vliet: None. G. Corbeil: None. M. Labrecque: None. M. Tétreault: None. I. Bourdeau: None. Introduction: Primary aldosteronism is a frequent cause of secondary hypertension in adults but is rare in children. We report the case and genetic studies of an 11 yo girl presenting with primary aldosteronism at puberty.

pmc-11549104.title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) for Esophagectomy: A Paradigm Shift in Perioperative Care
pmc-11549104.creator: Peter P Grimminger
pmc-11549104.description: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol offers a transformative approach to perioperative care, aimed at reducing surgical stress and symptom burden, thereby promoting rapid recovery and enhancing the quality of life for patients.1 The complexity of esophagectomy necessitates an optimal surgical model to mitigate the inherent risks and enhance patient outcomes.

pmc-12564793.title: Eight Years of Follow-Up of Rituximab in Pemphigus Vulgaris and Foliaceus at a Single Center: Assessing Efficacy and Safety in Light of Several Factors
pmc-12564793.creator: Konrad Szymanski, Cezary Kowalewski, Irena Walecka, Katarzyna Wozniak, Alan Fleischer
pmc-12564793.description: Background/Objectives: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) and foliaceus (PF) are autoimmune blistering diseases mediated by IgG antibodies directed against desmogleins 1 and 3 and are still considered life-threatening disorders. In recent years, rituximab has been shown to be very effective, especially in PV and mainly in short follow-ups.

pmc-12604673.title: Proliferative Necrotising Otitis Externa in a Cat Treated Successfully With Oclacitinib Maleate With Two Delayed Relapses
pmc-12604673.creator: Tian Chee, David Robson
pmc-12604673.description: This case report documents the successful treatment of a cat with proliferative necrotizing otitis externa (PNOE) using oclacitinib. Novel to this report, two episodes of delayed relapses occurred prior to complete spontaneous resolution, with an apparent dose‐dependent response to oclacitinib.
